title: Construction Engineering Technician
raw_text:
8-120A. Military Occupational Specialty 120A--Construction Engineering Technician
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 120A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are: 12H, 12K, 12N, 12P, 12Q,
   12R, 12T, or 12W, AIR FORCE 3E0xx, USMC 1169, 1361, 1141, NAVY BU, CE, UT, EA.
   d. Associated SQI.
       (1) O--No special qualifications.
       (2) 8--Instruction.
       (3) P--Parachutiste.
       (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
       (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASIs. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)). Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
   f. Qualifications.
      (1) WO1/CW2 must -
         (a) Successfully complete the Construction Engineering Technician Officer Warrant
Officer Basic Course.
         (b) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to the
Engineer Regiment, have normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, and have full use of both
hands.
         (c) Have good eye-hand coordination and manual dexterity to make minute adjustments
on sensitive instruments.
         (d) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
       (2) CW3 must -
           (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f (1) above.
           (b) Have successfully completed the Construction Engineering Technician Officer
Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
            (c) Successfully performed at the WO1/CW2 level.
       (3) CW4 –
           (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f (2) above.
           (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course.
           (c) Successfully perform at the CW3 level as described in paragraph g for the feeder
MOSs.
       (4) CW5-
          (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f (2) above.
          (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course.
          (c) Successfully perform at the CW3 level as described in paragraph g for the feeder
   g. Duties.
       (1) WO1 – CW2.
            (a) Serves as the Commander’s primary advisor on construction operations at company
and/or battalion levels.
            (b) Supervises and coordinates construction of base camps and internment facilities in
support of engineer construction operations.
            (c) Supervises the construction, repair, and maintenance of vertical infrastructure in
engineer construction operations.
            (d) Supervises and ensures proper preparation of a bill of materials, schedules of work
and ensures employment of proper safety procedures.
            (e) Devises network flow diagrams such as the critical path method and coordinates
work activities of supporting units.
            (f) Provide supervision over all structural and utility construction projects. Inspect
subordinate elements to ensure compliance with directives, construction drawings, specifications,
local codes and ordnances.
            (g) Serves as the Commander’s primary advisor in company level prime power
operations.
            (h) Provides advice and technical assistance on all aspects of electrical power and
distribution in support of military operations.
             (i) Supervises and manages separate teams in the performance of prime power
operations during disaster relief as a support element of FEMA and USACE and in theater level
operations.
            (j) Serves as Survey & Design Detachment Commander and primary advisor on
planning, preparation and execution of planning studies and tests for identified engineer work
projects. Addresses facility citing environmental concerns and estimated project costs.
            (k) Serves as Firefighting Headquarters Detachment Commander.
       (2) CW3.
           (a) Serves as the Battalion Maintenance Officer and Facilities Engineer in support of
Combat Support Hospital operations in non-operational and operational environments.
           (b) Primary advisor to the Commander and Staff on organizational maintenance support
of all equipment.
           (c) Provides engineering support and expertise on Deployable Medical Systems
(DEPMEDS), utilizing organic equipment such as power generation equipment, environment
control systems, water, waste, fuel and electrical distribution systems.
           (d) Coordinates and supervises the installation and repair of water supply systems,
plumbing, sewage, heating and air conditioning systems.
           (e) Serves as a Engineer Brigade Survey & Design Team staff officer and primary
advisor on planning, preparation and execution of planning studies and tests for identified
engineer work projects.
           (f) Addresses facility citing environmental concerns and estimated project costs.
           (g) Serves additionally as Service School Instructor / Writers in the revision of training
strategies, doctrine revisions, and formal engineering instruction to officers, warrant officers and
NCOs as an element of the United States Army Engineer School staff.
        (3) CW4.
             (a) Serves as a member of the Engineer Staff in operational and non-operational
MEBs, Division and Corps units.
             (b) Serves as the Commander’s primary advisor on all aspects of construction
operations, to include supervision of vertical and horizontal infrastructure and facilities
management.
             (c) Coordinates directly with DPW in construction project preparation, oversight and the
phased components of inspection for compliance with directives, construction drawings,
specifications, local codes and ordnances.
             (d) Serves as a member of the Installation Master Planning committee and monitors
MILCON project funding. Serves as the Prime Power Battalion Staff Officer and primary subject
matter expert on electrical power generation and distribution in support of global military
operations.
               (e) Serves as Service School Instructor / Writers in the revision of training strategies,
doctrine revisions, and formal engineering instruction to officers, warrant officers and NCOs as an
element of the United States Army Engineer School staff.
               (f) Serves additionally in the MOS immaterial positions of Proponency Coordinator
and Warrant Officer Career Branch Manager.
         (4) CW5.
              (a) Serves as the Construction Engineering expert and tactical and technical advisor to
the commander, staff and major subordinate commanders in the United States Army Engineer
School (USAES), United States Army Corps of Engineers and Army Service Component
Command.
              (b) Serves as the senior strategic advisor to the USAES Commandant in the capstone
nominative assignment of Regimental Chief Warrant Officer.
              (c) Serves as the Prime Power School Commander and primary advisor on the
education and production of the US Army Prime Power Specialist.
              (d) Serves additionally in the MOS immaterial position of Senior Warrant Officer
Advisor for the Combined Arms Center at Fort Leavenworth.
  g . Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
     (1) A physical demands rating of moderate (Gold).
     (2) Table 10-120A-1
      (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of three definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; and W4 equals CW4. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
         (a) Table 8-120A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (b) Table 8-120A-3. Standards of grade TDA.
     (4) Qualifying scores.
         (a) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs. and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles
in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
